extracted.intended_audience: installation commanders, contracting officers, Commercial Activity (A-76) study teams, and other DoD personnel involved in competitive sourcing
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and lessons-learned for planning, conducting, and managing A-76 competitive sourcing (commercial activity) studies at military installations, including PWS development, source selection, risk management, and post-decision actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Command support and leadership buy-in
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain and maintain support of the installation commander and ensure key leadership personnel 'buy into' the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize obtaining command support early; leadership should set the example for all members of the study group. Senior leadership needs to take an active role in the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Commercial Activities (CA) Team structured by functional areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize the CA Team into functional areas to examine requirements, then subdivide into teams (PWS, Management Plan, IGCE, QASP) to perform parallel tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: allows multiple tasks to be completed simultaneously while maintaining contact with the larger CA Team. Recommend forming an independent audit team to ensure all participants operate with a common baseline of data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use full-time participants and experienced personnel on CA Team
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed manning: utilize full-time participants for the A-76 study and bring in retired Civil Service employees for functional expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full-time members and retirees help collect accurate workload data and provide continuity and expertise; avoid relying solely on part-time staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiate team formulation before Congressional notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin formulation of the A-76 team once the process is known, but prior to Congressional notification so the team can start immediately once notification is given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows study work to begin promptly when the statutory clock starts running.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop open but controlled communication policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish communication channels for passing and receiving information to/from stakeholders without divulging information that could prejudice the MEO or offers or jeopardize the integrity of the A-76 process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance transparency with protection of competition; avoid sharing proprietary or prejudicial details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop detailed milestones and tracking system
rubrics_metrics.description: Create and track detailed milestones for each commercial activity under study, update promptly if schedules change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum recommended milestones: Begin development of the PWS and Management Plan; Complete first draft of the PWS; Complete PWS; Complete management study; Complete in-house cost estimate; Issue solicitation; Begin source selection process; Notify major commands of initial decision; Convene appeals board (if necessary); Begin transition period; Fully implement contractor operations or MEO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study whole functions rather than piecemeal components
rubrics_metrics.description: Commands should study an entire function (e.g., Public Works) to prevent studying only part of an activity and later wasting resources on additional studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial studies risk perpetuating inefficiency because the most efficient organization for the entire function would not be created or staffed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form a Commercial Activity Executive Committee and appoint a schedule lead
rubrics_metrics.description: Create an executive committee (Installation Commander as Chairman, directors of functions being studied, contracting officers, civilian personnel office, major commands) to monitor the study and make command decisions; appoint a single individual to keep the study moving per schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee provides oversight and decision-making authority; a named scheduler enforces timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish installation regulations and letters of instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish installation regulations relating to the A-76 process and letters of instruction outlining responsibilities and duties of action officers and participating organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies roles and responsibilities and helps enforce consistency and accountability during the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish an Acquisition Strategy Panel
rubrics_metrics.description: Form an Acquisition Strategy Panel at the beginning of the process to address commercial activity business strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issues for review include: contract type; use of contract incentives; use and disposition of Government property; desired performance factors; maintenance and/or replacement of property by Government or contractor; required interfaces with automated information management systems to ensure data collection for future contracts and HQ reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decide contract type early and gain concurrence
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose contract type early based on the nature of the work and obtain concurrence from interested parties before completing PWS and other contracting documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delaying decision on contract type can require rework of documents; do not begin final PWS and contracting documentation until contract type is settled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early determination and policy for unique labor sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Make early decisions about treatment of unique labor sources (prisoners, volunteers, borrowed military personnel) and develop a policy addressing their inclusion in the PWS, MEO, and cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unique labor creates challenges for workload accounting and comparisons; ground rules should be set early to avoid later disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect accurate workload data and analyze internal processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Take a fresh look at activities and analyze internal processes to identify inputs, outputs, and internal controls; avoid relying on prior performance studies as baseline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid adding tasks to surveys to stack the deck in favor of the in-house organization; accurate workload data prevents inflated PWS and ensures realistic contractor bids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct a Performance Requirements Review before finalizing PWS
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform a Performance Requirements Review prior to advancing other A-76 work, especially before finalizing the PWS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures the PWS accurately reflects actual work; prevents situations where contractor bids on inflated PWS leading to procurement upset and recompetition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use third-party review and validation of PWS requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a third party review and validate PWS requirements to ensure listed requirements are still performed and necessary, and operating procedures/frequency are current.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent validation helps detect inflated or outdated requirements and ensures reliability of baseline data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable Quality Levels (AQLs) in solicitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Solicitations should allow establishment of Allowable Quality Levels with reasonable levels of effort because most service contracts cannot be performed perfectly every time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define AQLs to set performance expectations and tolerances for defects or failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct PWS to state 'what' not 'how'; reserve methods to Section L/evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid prescribing how bidders must accomplish the work; state what work is required. If specific approaches are necessary, list them in Section L and include as evaluation criteria in the Source Selection Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tells bidders the required outcomes while preserving innovation; particular methods, if required, must be reflected in solicitation evaluation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use prior PWS templates with tailoring and caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Mixed guidance: avoid blindly copying prior PWSs, but templates can be used as a jumping-off point if individually tailored to current needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Templates can accelerate completion but must be adapted to avoid perpetuating irrelevant or inflated requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Involve contracting personnel in PWS development
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure contracting office personnel are involved in developing the PWS to provide knowledge of contract requirements that must be represented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting staff can help avoid later procurement problems and ensure contract clauses and data access requirements are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide database maintenance systems and Government access to performance data
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilize database systems capable of updating the PWS when workload changes occur, and require Government access to contractor-collected data on work performed and level-of-effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include data access and maintenance requirements in the PWS and relevant contract clauses to support future contracts and HQ reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure accurate workload data to avoid contract change orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Accurate workload data prevents work requirements from exceeding those outlined in the contract, which would otherwise require change orders and drive up contract price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careful workload measurement reduces cost risk and contractor disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop an in-depth Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP)
rubrics_metrics.description: QASP is vital for both fixed price and cost reimbursement contracts to control costs and ensure contractor performance meets specified performance levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: QASP helps discover discrepancies in the PWS that could raise contract price. Quality inspectors should not arbitrarily pick surveillance methods (e.g., random sampling); rely on functional personnel expertise to select appropriate surveillance methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perform cost comparisons between MEO and other bidders where applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Where competitions use MEO vs. contractor bids, perform cost comparison studies; note that some commands use direct conversion or may be in process of completing studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify when cost comparisons are appropriate; reasons for not performing comparisons include direct conversions, unfinished studies, or not applicable circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Integrated Product/Process Teams and a strong steering group
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ IPTs and a strong steering group to instill quality and enforce timelines; involve key management personnel most familiar with the function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPTs support both A-76 studies and direct conversions, and their involvement is frequently cited as critical to success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include contracting officer and local union early; keep employees informed
rubrics_metrics.description: Involve the contracting officer very early in the study process and include the local union; keep Government employees informed about the A-76 study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early involvement reduces later disputes and helps manage labor relations and transparency concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and plan to manage a broad range of risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify risk factors associated with A-76 such as: lack of qualified inspectors for QA evaluations; loss of in-house expertise; worker reaction/alienation; inability to capture workload data; difficulty finding a 'quality' contractor; minimum manpower shortfalls; SOW limitations; timelines and transition problems; protests; security clearance delays; IT manpower shortages; cost of studies; changing rules; unrealistic savings expectations; potential for delays; conflicts of interest and exposure to proprietary information; and 'massive upheaval' to mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents listed many specific risks and emphasized actions to manage them (training, leadership involvement, realistic timelines, early contracting action, careful PWS construction, third-party validation, and policy on unique labor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious about potential for protests and congressional/employee responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate protests or letters to Congress from affected parties; ensure costing processes and evaluations are defensible to withstand protests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain accurate, transparent costing; document methodology; involve stakeholders early to reduce grounds for protest; be prepared to explain and defend cost analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider 'Best Value' and use of incentives where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ 'Best Value' source selection approaches and consider use of incentives in competitive acquisitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best Value can be appropriate for competitive acquisitions; contracting strategy should consider incentives to achieve desired performance outcomes.
